title: Vibraphone
reference_instrument: Iowa MIS vibraphone (model NA; the page states neither the bar alloy, the resonator geometry nor whether the fan motor ran). C4 and E4 are compared with its sustained mf C4-B4 file; its pp and ff files give the ruler its other dynamic
summary: Two aluminium bars, C4 and E4, each over its own resonator tube: not yet a vibraphone. Each bar is a builder's design in EN AW-2017A, its undercut solved in the engine so the first partial sits at equal temperament on A4 = 442 Hz with f2 = 4 f1, over the builder's as-built tube. The tube couples now that the bar's own radiation damping comes from the engine: each mode's radiated power from the boundary-element solve, added as max(W, 0) over a loss row measured with the air pumped out, so the air counts once. A negative W is below the solve's resolution and adds nothing; the floor it sets is 4.75e-3 per second on C4 and 3.48e-3 on E4. With its tube each fundamental now decays faster than the recording's (C4 7.05 against 2.77 to 3.25 dB/s, E4 8.65 against 2.71 to 3.07), where the C4 bar alone decayed four to five times slower. The bars are not the recording's instrument, and the rubber mallet is a stand-in.
physics_present: Three-dimensional bars with the C4 and E4 outlines of a builder's F3-F6 vibraphone design (the Wyndorps DIY vibraphone pages: C4 323 x 57.15 x 12.0 mm, E4 303 x 50.8 x 12.0 mm, read from the builder's bar-set drawing), in EN AW-2017A aluminium with the Euralliage sheet's modulus, shear modulus, Poisson ratio and density, on a 56 x 6 x 3 mesh

A circular-arc undercut solved in the engine from the modes alone, for f1 at equal temperament on A4 = 442 Hz and f2 = 4 f1, the tuning rule a maker uses; 442 Hz is the tuning a maker prints for its M55-type vibraphones, and the grader's own read puts the recording's C4 to B4 within a few cents of it. The third mode is not aimed at

One loss factor on every bar mode, eta 8.340e-5, W. E. Howell's clean 2024-T4 aluminium beam 56 at 5.6e-4 atm (NASA TM X-2852, 1974): the beam's own loss with the air pumped out, from a thinner beam of a sister alloy, not a vibraphone bar

The bar's own radiation damping: each band mode's radiated power per unit modal velocity from the same Burton-Miller solve that gives the receiver, added to its loss as max(W, 0). Below the solve's resolution W comes out negative and adds nothing; the floor, the largest negative W, is printed beside the term: 4.75e-3 per second on C4 and 3.48e-3 on E4, where the third vertical modes' W are 4.35 and 11.1 per second

The builder's resonator tube under each bar, a column closed at the bottom (bore and air column inferred from the builder's CAD part: C4 radius 30 mm and 306.0 mm, E4 26.5 mm and 241.0 mm), its modes coupled to the bar's modes through the bar's boundary elements and radiating from its mouth as a free compact source
A Hertz contact mallet, the marimba cards' hard rubber row (Chaigne and Doutaut 1997) at 1.0 m/s, a declared stand-in on aluminium
Burton-Miller boundary-element radiation from the bar up to the band the card states, with no box, heard through the broadband observer
physics_missing: The right decay: with its tube coupled, each fundamental decays faster than the recording's: C4 at 7.05 dB/s (T60 8.5 s) against 2.77 to 3.25 dB/s (T60 18 to 22 s, three strikes), E4 at 8.65 dB/s (T60 6.9 s) against 2.71 to 3.07 dB/s (two strikes). How much of the tube's loss each fundamental takes is set by the tube's wall and open-end losses and by the bar-to-tube gap, which is not printed and is a 12.7 mm stand-in. Viscous air loss on the bar, the support cords and felts and the mallet's contact loss are not modelled, and nothing is adjusted to close the gap

Radiation damping finer than the boundary-element solve resolves: a mode whose W comes out negative gets none, and the far-field radiated power is not computed. The modes the pages rest on sit well above the floor, except C4's 1051.3 Hz mode at 4.9 times it, which adds 0.20 dB/s to that partial's 2.60 dB/s
The recording's mallet: vibraphone mallets are usually cord- or yarn-wrapped and the recording names none; the hard rubber stand-in is not it
The fan valves that give the vibraphone its vibrato: not modelled. The recording's notes carry no envelope modulation at one rate common to all of them, so its motor was off
A measured vibraphone bar: the undercut is solved from the tuning rule, not measured, and the recording's bar alloy and outline are not stated
Neighbouring bars, the frame and the damper

A second take: the ruler compares the recording's other dynamics of the same note and its neighbouring notes, and has no other take of the note, since the Iowa page carries one take of each note at each dynamic
The recording's other notes from C4 to B4: A4's undercut is still being solved, and the others have no card yet
